title: Test whether you have product-market fit
summary: Early start-ups live or die on product-market fit. Measure it directly, find who loves the product most, and build for them.

beginner: Ask active users: how would you feel if you could no longer use this product?
Count the share who answer very disappointed.
Look at who those users are and what they value most.
Ask the others what would make the product better for them.
Repeat the survey regularly and track the share over time.
intermediate: Segment results to find your highest-expectation customers.
Split the roadmap between what fans love and what holds others back.
Track the product-market fit score alongside retention.
experienced: Use the score to decide whether to scale, refocus or pivot.
Run the survey for each new segment or market you enter.
Share the results with the founders and investors as a standing measure.

toolExamples.google-docs: Run the survey with a simple form and keep results in a sheet.
toolExamples.amplitude: Compare usage of very disappointed users with others.

definitionOfDone: Roadmap changes agreed from the results
pitfalls: Surveying people who barely used the product
Building for everyone instead of the fans

leaderView.good: Start-ups measure product-market fit directly and focus on the users who love the product most.
ask: How would users feel if they could no longer use the product?
Who are our most engaged users, and what do they have in common?
signs: Growth is pushed before fit is proven.
The target user changes every month.
